content_units: Credit Card Payoff Snapshot
You have   $8,400   across 3 cards, with   $260/month in minimums   plus   $500 extra  , so total planned payment is   $760/month  .
With no new card spending, all three strategies fully pay off the debt in roughly the   same overall timeframe: about 13 months  . The real difference is   interest cost   and   motivation flow  .
Strategy Comparison for Your 3 Cards
Formula: Monthly interest \(\approx \text{balance} \times \frac{\text{APR}}{12}\)
Strategy   Payoff Order   Estimated Total Interest   Estimated Payoff Time   Best For
Avalanche   Card C (29%) → Card A (24%) → Card B (18%)     About $915       About 13 months     Lowest interest cost
Snowball   Card C ($900) → Card A ($2,400) → Card B ($5,100)     About $915       About 13 months     Fast early wins
Hybrid   Card C first, then avalanche     About $915       About 13 months     Same as avalanche here
Why avalanche and hybrid match here:
-   Card C is both the highest APR and the smallest balance  , so both methods start the same way.
- After Card C, the next highest APR is   Card A  , then   Card B  , which also happens to be the same order as snowball once C is gone.
- So in   this specific debt set  , all 3 methods end up following essentially the   same payoff sequence  .
Best Choice for Interest vs Motivation
Lowest-interest winner
Avalanche   saves the most interest — but here it is effectively tied with the hybrid and snowball because the debt order overlaps almost perfectly.
Easiest psychologically
Snowball   is usually the easiest psychologically because:
- you eliminate a balance quickly
- you get a visible early win
- the plan feels simpler and more motivating

But in your case, that psychological advantage is also muted because   avalanche already starts with the smallest card  . So you get the emotional win of killing Card C first   without giving up interest savings  .
Practical recommendation
Use   avalanche   and think of it as:
-   Kill Card C first
- then   Card A
- then   Card B
That gives you:
- the   lowest possible interest
- the   same first quick win   a snowball user would get
- a very simple monthly plan
Month-by-Month Direction
Option 1:   Avalanche / Hybrid Plan     Best overall fit for this debt mix   Lowest-cost path
- Pay minimums on all cards.
- Send the full   $500 extra   to   Card C   first.
- After Card C is cleared, roll its freed payment into   Card A  .
- Then roll everything into   Card B  .
Option 2:   Snowball Plan     Best if motivation matters most   Same practical order here
- Pay minimums on all cards.
- Attack the   smallest balance first: Card C  .
- Then move to   Card A  , then   Card B  .
- In this case, it behaves almost the same as avalanche.
Key Takeaways for Your Debt Mix
-   Most interest saved:     Avalanche
-   Easiest psychologically:     Snowball
-   Best real-world choice here:     Avalanche  , because it gives you the same first quick win as snowball
-   Hybrid result:   effectively   the same as avalanche   for these balances/APRs
- Estimated total interest across all approaches is   very close to identical, around $915
Calculation Notes
Using standard monthly APR/12 interest with fixed total payment of   $760/month  :
- Card A:   $2,400 at 24% APR  , minimum   $72
- Card B:   $5,100 at 18% APR  , minimum   $153
- Card C:   $900 at 29% APR  , minimum   $35
- Extra monthly payment:   $500
- No new spending assumed
If you want the cleanest rule to follow each month, use this:
-   Pay $572 to Card C and minimums to A and B
- then   pay $607 to Card A and minimum to B
- then   pay everything to Card B
